analysis.title: Fed holds rates steady despite inflation being too high
key_insights: The Fed voted 10-2 to hold the Fed funds target range at 3.75%-4%. Only 2bp of a 25bp hike was priced ahead of the decision, and only 6 of 97 organisations polled by Bloomberg predicted a hike, so market reaction was limited.

Beth Hammack and Lisa Cook dissented in favour of a further hike. Cook's vote was a surprise given her reputation as a centrist. ING had expected Neel Kashkari and/or Lorrie Logan, who both dissented in July, to join Hammack.

The statement changed little. It describes the economy as 'expanding at a strong pace' and says 'inflation remains elevated'. It makes no pre-commitment to further action and says data will determine the policy stance.

Chair Warsh gave no real guidance beyond saying inflation remains too high. He said the overwhelming consensus in the FOMC is that the 'medicine' is starting to work, and that the Fed will deliver price stability, 'no ifs, ands or buts'.
From next September one FOMC meeting a year will have no rate vote and will focus on monetary policy strategy. From 2028 two meetings will do so, leaving six meetings with rate decisions.

ING's base case is a 25bp hike in December, taking the range to 4.00%-4.25%. ING calls it a solid bet. Warsh declined to give a prediction and noted that policy accommodation was already removed in September.

Two jobs reports and one inflation print come before the December decision. November CPI is released the day after the Fed meeting and officials will almost certainly see it first, so a surprise cannot be ruled out.

ING's Fed path assumes an energy deal after the midterms that improves Persian Gulf flows and sharply cuts shipping and insurance costs. ING sees that as the key to lower pump prices while refineries run at capacity.

ING sees US inflation returning to 2% in H2 2027, helped by wage growth of 3% and further housing disinflation (housing is 35% of the inflation basket). It expects a prolonged pause through December 2027, when the December 2026 hike is reversed.
ING's Fed forecast matches the current consensus. The Fed's own projections show one hike this year and no change through 2027.

The 10-year Treasury yield had been holding at about 4.99% before the meeting. It rose initially, then fell back to 5% and briefly below during the press conference on Warsh's comments that inflation expectations had been tamed somewhat.
ING says inflation expectations rose after the decision and Warsh's remarks. It sees this as enough to validate the 10-year yield moving back above 5%, and keeps its view of a move toward 5.25%.

The implementation note was broadly unchanged. Implementation rates and mechanisms are unchanged and the Fed keeps reinvesting MBS principal payments into Treasury bills. A balance sheet shrinkage plan, a stated Warsh objective, is likely still some way off, with committee recommendations expected near the turn of the year.
Liquidity conditions are stable, with repo functioning far better than a year ago.

The dollar softened slightly after the lack of December guidance weighed on short-dated rates. ING attributes this to positioning after a one-way run higher since early September, driven by energy prices, solid US activity and French budget problems.
ING expects the dollar to consolidate toward the top of recent ranges unless the ECB (Thursday) or Bank of Japan (Friday) meetings deliver major hawkish surprises.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed held rates in a 10-2 vote with two dissents for a hike. Markets had priced almost no chance of a hike.
ING expects a 25bp hike in December. Hawkish pressure on front-end rates and the dollar depends on the November CPI and jobs data.
ING expects a prolonged pause and then the hike reversed, in line with consensus.
The yield held about 4.99% before the meeting, moved above 5%, and returned to 5% and briefly below during the press conference.
ING expects the yield to keep trending toward 5.25%.
ING describes wage growth as benign, which supports its disinflation view.
ING expects inflation to return to the Fed's goal in H2 2027 if energy shipping costs ease.

risk_factors: November CPI is released the day after the Fed meeting, so officials see it before the market does and could surprise.
No agreement on Persian Gulf energy flows and shipping costs would delay the fall in pump prices and inflation.
Rising inflation expectations after the decision.
Tighter financial conditions from higher Treasury yields and a firmer dollar.
Hawkish surprises from the ECB or Bank of Japan could change the dollar outlook.
vol_and_positioning: Only 2bp of a 25bp hike was priced before the decision.
The dollar has seen one-way positioning since early September, and the slight softening after the meeting probably reflects that positioning.
geopolitical: An agreement improving energy flows from the Persian Gulf and cutting shipping and insurance costs is assumed by ING in the months after the midterm elections.
French budget problems cited as a driver of dollar strength since early September.
Fraught relationship between President Trump and Fed Governor Lisa Cook.

tension_points.bull_case: ING sees a December hike as a solid bet. A majority of FOMC members project a hike before year-end, inflation expectations rose after the meeting, and the Fed has said it will deliver price stability.
tension_points.bear_case: Senior officials including Jefferson, Bowman and Waller said they saw little need for back-to-back hikes. Warsh gave no guidance, said inflation is going the right way and that policy was already tightened in September.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A soft November CPI, released the day after the Fed meeting, or weaker jobs reports before the December decision.

theme_stances.key_argument: A majority of FOMC members project a hike this year and inflation remains too high, so a December hike is the most likely path.
theme_stances.evidence: a December hike looks a solid bet

theme_stances.key_argument: The hawkish statement and rising inflation expectations validate the move back above 5% and a path toward 5.25%.
theme_stances.evidence: enough to validate the move back above 5% on the 10yr

theme_stances.key_argument: Strong, broadening US growth and above-target inflation mean the dollar does not need to correct much.
theme_stances.evidence: the dollar does not need to correct much at all
